Entertainment / Behind the screen

Watch with your ears: noticing film sound

An invitation to hear the world around the dialogue.

✳
The Offbeat EditCulture Issue · 1 min read

IN THIS STORY

Start with the roomNotice the handoverReturn to the whole sceneMore from Entertainment

Start with the room

Listen to the space a scene creates. Footsteps, distant traffic, or a quiet electrical hum can make a location feel inhabited before anyone explains where you are.

Choose a scene you can replay legally and listen at a comfortable volume. You do not need specialist equipment to notice a change between a crowded room and an empty corridor.

Notice the handover

A sound can arrive before its image or continue after a cut. Watch for the point where your attention moves. Does the transition feel abrupt, gentle, or strangely unsettled?

Avoid assuming every sound was captured during filming. The finished soundtrack is a constructed experience, and credits or official production notes are better guides to the process than a guess.

Return to the whole scene

After concentrating on sound, watch normally again. The exercise is useful if it makes the scene feel richer, not if it turns every moment into an assignment.

Bring one observation to a conversation about the film. Describing what you heard can open up a different discussion from simply deciding whether you liked it.

“An invitation to hear the world around the dialogue.”
